eli5: The simplest recipe: chop text into pieces, find the pieces most similar to your question, and feed them to the AI to write an answer.
purpose: Establish a baseline retrieval-augmented generation pipeline by mapping unstructured text to dense vector embeddings for semantic similarity search.
input_dataset: Unstructured text documents, PDFs, or web pages.
usecase_scenarios: Simple internal FAQ bots
Basic document Q&A for small knowledge bases
Rapid prototyping and MVP development
outcome: Context-aware LLM responses grounded in the most semantically similar retrieved text chunks.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(N) for indexing, O(log N) for vector search, O(1) for generation
pros: Extremely fast to implement and deploy
Low infrastructure and compute costs
Works surprisingly well for simple, direct queries
cons: Highly sensitive to chunk boundaries (loss of context)
Fails on complex, multi-context, or ambiguous queries
No mechanism to verify if retrieved context is actually relevant
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Automate ingestion using semantic chunkers instead of fixed-size splits. 2) Use Ragas or DeepEval to automatically benchmark the baseline. 3) For open-source deployments, host the embedding model on local NPUs for cost-effective inference.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-V3 for generation; its strong instruction following makes it highly robust to slightly noisy naive retrieval contexts.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is the perfect open-source model to run locally for the generation step, offering enterprise-grade quality at a fraction of the cost.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's native long context means you can often skip Naive RAG entirely and just pass the whole document if it's under 128k tokens.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4-Flash provides ultra-low latency for the generation step, making Naive RAG feel instantaneous for high-throughput internal tools.

references: Lewis et al. 2020 'Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks'

eli5: Upgrades the basic recipe by cleaning up the question before searching, filtering out bad results, and squishing the good results to save space.
purpose: Maximize retrieval precision and generation quality in production by applying pre-retrieval, retrieval, and post-retrieval optimizations.
input_dataset: Unstructured documents with rich metadata.
usecase_scenarios: Enterprise search where accuracy is critical
Noisy document repositories
Regulated industries requiring strict metadata filtering
outcome: Highly precise, context-compressed inputs to the LLM, drastically reducing hallucinations and token costs.
benchmark_metrics: Token compression ratio without faithfulness loss

metadata.computational_complexity: O(N) for retrieval + O(K log K) for re-ranking + O(C) for compression
pros: Significantly boosts retrieval accuracy
Reduces LLM context window usage via compression
Handles edge-case queries gracefully
cons: Increases end-to-end latency
Requires tuning multiple models
Higher infrastructure footprint
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Use DSPy to automatically optimize query rewriting prompts. 2) Automate re-ranker selection via A/B testing. 3) Implement LongLLMLingua for automated context compression. 4) Deploy BGE-Reranker on local infrastructure to avoid external API dependencies.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-R1's extended thinking can be used as the 'query rewriter' to deeply analyze and decompose complex user queries before retrieval.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5-14B makes an excellent, highly efficient local re-ranker and query rewriter, keeping the entire Advanced RAG pipeline on-premise.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's massive context allows you to skip the compression step entirely; just pass the top 20 raw chunks to Kimi and let it figure it out.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's strong bilingual capabilities make it ideal for Advanced RAG in mixed-language enterprise environments.

references: Gao et al. 2023 'Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey'

eli5: Searches for both the exact words you typed and the general meaning of your question, then combines the best matches from both.
purpose: Overcome the limitations of pure dense vector search by fusing lexical (BM25) and semantic (dense) retrieval.
input_dataset: Unstructured text containing specific identifiers, error codes, SKUs, or technical jargon.
usecase_scenarios: Technical support bots searching for specific error codes
E-commerce product search
Legal and medical document retrieval
outcome: A unified, highly relevant set of documents capturing both exact keyword matches and conceptual semantic similarities.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(N) for BM25 + O(log N) for Vector Search + O(K) for fusion
pros: Solves the 'out of vocabulary' weakness of pure vector DBs
Massively improves recall for specific queries
Robust against embedding model blind spots
cons: Requires maintaining two index structures
Tuning fusion weights can be tricky
Higher storage requirements
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Automate weight tuning using Bayesian Optimization on a validation set. 2) Use Qdrant or Weaviate to automate hybrid search natively. 3) Implement automated query classification to dynamically adjust weights.
dependencies: Sparse Embedding Model or BM25 Index

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek handles hybrid context exceptionally well. Instruct it via system prompt to prioritize exact matches for IDs and semantic matches for concepts.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5's strong multilingual tokenizer ensures that BM25 lexical matching works flawlessly across CJK and Latin scripts simultaneously.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's long context makes Hybrid RAG highly effective when searching across thousands of distinct documents.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's function calling can dynamically decide whether to execute a pure SQL/BM25 exact match or a Vector semantic search.

references: Luan et al. 2021 'Generalized Product Quantization Network for Semantic Retrieval'

eli5: Instead of trying to answer a hard question all at once, the AI breaks it down into smaller questions, answers them one by one, and pieces the answers together.
purpose: Resolve complex, multi-step queries that require retrieving and synthesizing information from multiple disparate documents.
input_dataset: Large, diverse document collections where answers are distributed across multiple sources.
usecase_scenarios: Comparative analysis across different entities
Complex investigative queries
Multi-document summarization
outcome: Comprehensive, logically deduced answers connecting information across multiple retrieval hops.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(H * (N + L)) where H is hops
pros: Solves complex reasoning tasks that fail in single-hop RAG
Mimics human analytical research behavior
Highly accurate for comparative queries
cons: Very high latency and API costs
Prone to error propagation
Complex to debug
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Use LangGraph to automate the state machine for multi-hop reasoning. 2) Implement DSPy's multi_hop optimizer to tune decomposition prompts. 3) Add an automated 'confidence check' at each hop to trigger self-correction.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-R1 is the undisputed king of Multi-hop RAG. Its extended thinking allows it to explicitly plan the hops, evaluate intermediate results, and correct its own reasoning path natively.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct provides excellent multi-hop reasoning capabilities and can be hosted locally to avoid high API costs.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's 'Kimi Explorer' feature natively performs deep, multi-hop web and document search, making it a turnkey solution.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's strong logical reasoning and tool-use capabilities allow it to reliably chain multiple retrieval tools without losing the thread.

references: Xiong et al. 2022 'Answering Complex Open-domain Questions Through Iterative Query Generation'

eli5: Instead of just looking at text, it builds a map of 'who/what is connected to whom' and uses that map to find answers about relationships and dependencies.
purpose: Retrieve and reason over complex, interconnected data by leveraging knowledge graphs rather than relying solely on raw text similarity.
input_dataset: Unstructured text that can be parsed into entities and relationships.
usecase_scenarios: Supply chain and dependency mapping
Organizational and hierarchical queries
Biological pathways synthesis
outcome: Answers that accurately reflect structural dependencies, hierarchies, and global community contexts.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(N * L) for graph extraction, O(V + E) for traversal
pros: Unmatched at reasoning over relationships and dependencies
Provides global context via community summaries
Highly explainable and auditable
cons: Extremely high initial compute cost for graph extraction
Entity extraction can be noisy
Requires specialized graph database knowledge
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Automate graph construction using LlamaIndex's PropertyGraphIndex. 2) Use Microsoft's GraphRAG pipeline for community detection. 3) Implement a hybrid Graph+Vector approach. 4) Use local models to handle the heavy LLM load of entity extraction.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-V3 excels at generating valid, complex Cypher queries from natural language. Use it to translate user queries into graph traversals.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5 is highly cost-effective for the massive entity-extraction phase of GraphRAG indexing, especially for multilingual datasets.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's massive context window is perfect for ingesting the massive 'community summaries' generated by Microsoft GraphRAG without truncation.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's robust tool-use can dynamically decide whether a query requires a graph traversal (Cypher) or a standard vector search.

references: Edge et al. 2024 'From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization'

eli5: Reads the table of contents and summaries first to find the right chapter, then dives into the specific paragraphs in that chapter to get the exact details.
purpose: Preserve broad document context while retrieving specific details by indexing and retrieving at multiple levels of granularity.
input_dataset: Very large, highly structured documents (books, long reports, legal contracts, codebases).
usecase_scenarios: Analyzing 100+ page financial reports
Codebase understanding
Scenarios where surrounding context is critical
outcome: Highly contextualized responses where the LLM understands both micro-details and macro-structure.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(N) for multi-level indexing, O(log N) for hierarchical search
pros: Prevents context fragmentation problems
Allows for broad-to-narrow retrieval strategies
Improves LLM comprehension of document structure
cons: Complex indexing strategy
Higher storage requirements
Slower retrieval due to two-step resolution
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Automate document parsing using Unstructured.io. 2) Use LlamaIndex's AutoMergingRetriever to automatically merge child chunks. 3) Implement an automated background job to regenerate summaries when parent documents update.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-Coder-V2 is exceptional for Hierarchical RAG on codebases, understanding the file-to-function hierarchy better than almost any other model.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5's strong structural understanding makes it ideal for generating the parent-level summaries during the indexing phase.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's 2M context window makes Hierarchical RAG largely obsolete for single documents; you can just feed the whole book to Kimi.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's document parsing capabilities make it excellent at extracting the natural hierarchical boundaries (headers, sections) during ingestion.

references: Ma et al. 2023 'RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval'

eli5: The AI checks its own homework. If the documents it found don't actually answer the question, it throws them out and searches somewhere else before answering.
purpose: Introduce a verification layer that evaluates the relevance of retrieved documents, triggering corrective actions if the internal retrieval is deemed insufficient.
input_dataset: Internal knowledge base + optional external search API.
usecase_scenarios: Mission-critical applications where hallucinations are unacceptable
Dynamic knowledge bases where internal data might be outdated
Customer-facing bots requiring high factual reliability
outcome: Validated, high-confidence context passed to the generator, drastically reducing hallucinations.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(N) for retrieval + O(1) for grading + O(W) for web fallback
pros: Self-correcting mechanism drastically reduces hallucinations
Ensures only high-quality context reaches the generator
Gracefully handles knowledge cutoffs
cons: Adds significant latency
Increases API/LLM costs
Grading prompts must be meticulously tuned
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Automate the grading threshold using Ragas. 2) Use a lightweight, fine-tuned classifier instead of a full LLM for the evaluation step to reduce latency. 3) Implement LangGraph for conditional routing.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: Use DeepSeek-V3 for the final generation, but use a smaller, faster model (like Qwen2.5-7B) for the retrieval grading step to minimize latency and cost.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5-7B is the perfect open-source 'grader' model. It's fast, cheap to host locally, and highly accurate at evaluating retrieval relevance.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's built-in web search integration makes the 'fallback' step of CRAG seamless and highly reliable without needing external APIs.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's strong safety and alignment training makes it an excellent, conservative 'grader' that will reliably reject hallucinated or irrelevant context.

references: Yan et al. 2024 'Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation'

from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
def grade_documents(state):
    return 'correct' if score > threshold else 'incorrect'
workflow = StateGraph(State)
workflow.add_node('retrieve', retrieve_docs)
workflow.add_node('grade', grade_docs)
workflow.add_conditional_edges('grade', grade_documents, {'correct': 'generate', 'incorrect': 'web_search'})

eli5: The AI is trained to pause and think: 'Do I need to look this up?', 'Does this look-up actually help?', and 'Did I just make up this answer?' before speaking.
purpose: Empower the LLM with intrinsic self-reflection capabilities, allowing it to autonomously decide when to retrieve, evaluate relevance, and critique its own generation.
input_dataset: Unstructured text + fine-tuning data for reflection tokens (or specialized prompting).
usecase_scenarios: Answer grounding where strict adherence to evidence is required
Reducing hallucinations without sacrificing fluency
Optimizing retrieval costs by only retrieving when necessary
outcome: Highly grounded, factually accurate outputs with built-in self-correction.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(N) for retrieval (conditional) + O(L) for generation with reflection
pros: Highly grounded and factually accurate
Dynamic retrieval saves compute
Built-in self-correction
cons: Requires complex prompting or specific fine-tuning
Slower generation due to reflection steps
Reflection tokens can disrupt natural output flow
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Use DSPy to automatically optimize complex system prompts that simulate Self-RAG reflection steps. 2) Automate the evaluation of reflection quality using a secondary LLM judge. 3) Combine with CRAG for external validation.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-R1's native 'extended thinking' is the ultimate Self-RAG implementation. It naturally outputs its retrieval decisions, relevance checks, and support verification in its thinking blocks.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5 can be prompted to output structured JSON reflection steps (e.g., {'needs_retrieval': true}) to simulate Self-RAG without fine-tuning.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's long context reduces the need for the 'needs retrieval' check, but its strong instruction following makes it great at the 'is_supported' critique phase.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's structured output capabilities ensure that the reflection tokens or JSON critique steps are generated reliably without breaking the pipeline.

references: Asai et al. 2023 'Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection'
metadata.code_snippet:
self_rag_prompt = """
Answer the question. 
1. Output [Retrieve] if you need external info.
2. After retrieving, output [IsRelevant: Yes/No].
3. Generate answer.
4. Output [IsSupported: Yes/No] based on retrieved text.
"""
response = llm.invoke(self_rag_prompt + user_query)

eli5: Instead of a fixed assembly line, you give the AI a toolbox and let it decide which tools to use, in what order, and when to stop, to solve the problem.
purpose: Transform RAG from a fixed pipeline into a dynamic, autonomous workflow where an AI agent decides when to retrieve, which tools to call, and whether to iterate.
input_dataset: Multi-modal data sources: Vector DBs, SQL databases, REST APIs, Web Search.
usecase_scenarios: Complex tasks requiring multiple data sources
Dynamic workflows where the retrieval strategy cannot be predetermined
Systems requiring autonomous problem-solving
outcome: Autonomously executed, multi-step workflows that seamlessly integrate structured and unstructured data.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(I * (T + L)) where I is iterations
pros: Ultimate flexibility
Seamlessly integrates structured and unstructured data
Can perform actions beyond retrieval
cons: Unpredictable execution paths make debugging difficult
Very high latency and compute costs
Risk of infinite loops
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Use LangGraph to build stateful, cyclic agent workflows with checkpointing. 2) Automate tool selection using DSPy's ReAct optimizers. 3) Implement strict guardrails: max iteration limits, token budget caps, and automated observability.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-V3 has top-tier native tool-use (function calling) capabilities. Use its native JSON tool calling rather than parsing text to ensure 100% reliable execution.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct is currently one of the best open-source models for Agentic RAG, rivaling closed models in complex multi-tool orchestration.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's 'Kimi Explorer' acts as a pre-built Agentic RAG system for web and document research, requiring zero setup for basic autonomous search tasks.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's Agent framework (AutoGLM) provides built-in orchestration for complex, multi-step tool use, making it highly effective for desktop and web automation.

references: Wang et al. 2023 'Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models'

eli5: The AI remembers what you talked about yesterday and what you like, combining that personal history with new information to give you a customized answer.
purpose: Enhance RAG by incorporating relevant information from previous user interactions or stored long-term memory alongside external knowledge for personalized responses.
input_dataset: External knowledge base + User interaction history / Profile data.
usecase_scenarios: Personalized AI assistants and customer support bots
Conversations that span multiple sessions
Applications requiring the AI to 'remember' user preferences
outcome: Highly personalized, continuous user experiences where the AI adapts based on historical context.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(M) for memory retrieval + O(N) for knowledge retrieval + O(L) for generation
pros: Creates a highly personalized experience
Reduces need for users to repeat context
Improves relevance via user history
cons: Complex memory management
Significant privacy and security concerns
Risk of over-indexing on past interactions
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Use a dedicated memory layer like Mem0 or Zep. 2) Implement automated 'memory decay' via background cron jobs. 3) Ensure strict data isolation and use highly encrypted open-source authentication to secure user memory stores.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek's strong instruction following ensures it strictly adheres to the boundary between 'user preferences' (memory) and 'objective facts' (retrieved docs).
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5's excellent multilingual capabilities allow it to maintain and retrieve user memories accurately across different languages in global deployments.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's massive context window allows you to inject the entire user interaction history directly into the prompt, bypassing the need for a separate memory retrieval step for short histories.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's strong alignment and safety features make it highly reliable at handling sensitive user memory data without leaking it or hallucinating personal details.

references: Park et al. 2023 'Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior'

eli5: Before chopping the document into pieces, the AI reads the whole thing and rewrites each piece to include the missing context, so the chopped piece makes sense on its own.
purpose: Improve embedding quality and retrieval accuracy by prepending document-level context to each chunk before embedding.
input_dataset: Unstructured text documents where chunks lack standalone semantic meaning.
usecase_scenarios: Highly technical documents where isolated chunks are ambiguous
Financial reports where 'Q1 Revenue' needs to be contextualized
Legal contracts where clauses depend on the preamble
outcome: Dense embeddings that capture both the micro-content of the chunk and the macro-context of the document.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(N * L) for contextual rewriting, O(log N) for search
pros: Massively improves retrieval accuracy for ambiguous chunks
Reduces the need for complex post-retrieval re-ranking
Works with any standard vector database
cons: High one-time compute cost for indexing
Increases the size of the embedded text
Requires a reliable, fast LLM for the rewriting step
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Use a fast, cheap model to generate the contextual prefixes. 2) Automate the pipeline: Parse -> Chunk -> LLM Rewrite -> Embed. 3) Use DSPy to optimize the prompt that generates the contextual prefix.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: Use DeepSeek-V3 for the contextual rewriting step if quality is paramount; its instruction following ensures the context is added smoothly.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is the absolute best choice for this pattern. It's fast, cheap to host locally, and highly capable of generating concise contextual prefixes.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's massive context allows it to read the entire document at once and generate highly accurate, globally consistent contextual prefixes for every chunk.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4-Flash provides ultra-low latency and high throughput for the contextual rewriting step, making it ideal for processing massive document repositories quickly.

references: Anthropic 2024 'Introducing Contextual Retrieval'
metadata.code_snippet:

eli5: Instead of searching for the answer every time, you read the entire book once, memorize it, and then just answer questions directly from your memory instantly.
purpose: Bypass the retrieval step entirely at inference time by pre-loading all relevant documents into the LLM's Key-Value (KV) cache.
input_dataset: Small to medium-sized, fixed document sets.
usecase_scenarios: Customer support bots for a specific product line
Interactive fiction with a fixed lore book
High-throughput scenarios where retrieval latency is unacceptable
outcome: Instantaneous, highly accurate LLM responses with zero retrieval latency.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(N) for initial KV cache preloading, O(1) for retrieval, O(L) for generation
pros: Zero retrieval latency at inference time
Eliminates retrieval errors caused by bad chunking
Simplifies architecture
cons: Limited by the model's maximum context window
High VRAM usage for storing the KV cache
Not suitable for dynamic or massive datasets
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Use vLLM with --enable-prefix-caching or SGLang with RadixAttention. 2) Quantize the KV cache (e.g., FP8) to reduce VRAM usage. 3) Only use CAG when the total document size is well within the model's context limit.
dependencies: Inference Engine with KV Cache Management

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-V3's Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) drastically reduces the VRAM footprint of the KV cache, making CAG highly viable for much larger document sets.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5's native 128k (and up to 1M) context window, combined with its efficient attention mechanisms, makes it a perfect candidate for CAG.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's 2M context window is the ultimate CAG engine. You can literally load entire codebases or hundreds of books into the context and skip retrieval entirely.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's long context support allows for effective CAG on standard business documents, and its optimized inference stack ensures the pre-loaded context doesn't bottleneck generation speed.

references: vLLM Documentation: Prefix Caching

eli5: The AI doesn't just read text; it looks at pictures, charts, and diagrams, and can find answers hidden inside the images just as well as in the text.
purpose: Extend RAG beyond text by embedding and retrieving multimodal data (images, charts, tables) alongside text.
input_dataset: Documents containing mixed media: PDFs with charts, presentations, technical manuals.
usecase_scenarios: Analyzing financial reports with complex charts
Technical support for hardware with visual diagrams
Geospatial analysis involving satellite imagery
outcome: Comprehensive answers that synthesize both textual data and visual evidence.

pros: Unlocks critical information trapped in images and tables
Provides a more complete context for the LLM
Essential for technical and scientific domains

Requires specialized multimodal embedding models
Complex pipeline setup
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Use Unstructured.io or LlamaParse to automatically extract images and tables. 2) Use a multimodal embedding model or generate text captions for images before embedding. 3) For advanced setups, use ColPali for direct vision-to-text retrieval.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-VL2 is exceptionally strong at understanding complex charts, diagrams, and scientific figures. Use it as the generation engine to interpret retrieved visual context.

model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's native PDF parser is highly optimized for extracting tables and charts from complex documents, making the ingestion phase of Multimodal RAG seamless.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4V is highly optimized for visual question answering and diagram retrieval. Its strong bilingual capabilities make it ideal for multimodal RAG in diverse linguistic environments.

usecase_scenarios: Real-time crop productivity monitoring
Supply chain disruption analysis based on weather and location
Urban planning and infrastructure maintenance Q&A
outcome: Highly precise, location-aware answers that respect geographical boundaries and semantic meaning simultaneously.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(S) for spatial index search + O(log N) for vector search + O(K) for fusion
pros: Solves the critical 'where' dimension missing in standard RAG
Drastically reduces irrelevant context by enforcing spatial boundaries
Enables complex spatial reasoning
cons: Requires specialized spatial database knowledge
Complex query formulation
Higher infrastructure complexity
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Use PostGIS with pgvector for a unified spatial-vector database. 2) Index geospatial metadata using H3 hexagonal grids. 3) Implement a two-step retrieval: first filter by spatial bounding box, then perform vector similarity search. 4) Use LLMs to translate natural language spatial queries into PostGIS SQL.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-Coder-V2 is exceptional at generating complex PostGIS SQL queries with spatial joins from natural language, making the retrieval step highly accurate.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5's strong multilingual and geospatial reasoning capabilities make it ideal for processing global POI data and generating spatial queries in diverse languages.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's massive context is perfect for ingesting massive geospatial text reports and combining them with spatial metadata.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's robust tool-use can orchestrate the GeoRAG pipeline: calling a spatial API to get the bounding box, then querying the vector DB, and finally synthesizing the result.

references: PostGIS Documentation: Spatial Indexing

algorithm_name: Late Interaction RAG / ColBERTv2 Token-Level Matching
eli5: Instead of squishing a whole paragraph into one single number to compare, it compares every single word in your question to every single word in the paragraph to find the exact matches.
purpose: Achieve state-of-the-art retrieval accuracy by using late interaction (token-level matching) instead of single-vector dot products.
input_dataset: Large-scale unstructured text where fine-grained matching is critical.
usecase_scenarios: High-stakes legal discovery
Medical literature retrieval
Complex technical documentation
outcome: Exceptionally high retrieval precision and recall, outperforming standard dense vector search.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(N * L_q * L_d) for scoring, requires specialized indexing for O(1) inference
pros: State-of-the-art retrieval accuracy
Captures fine-grained nuances
Highly robust to out-of-vocabulary terms
cons: Massive storage overhead
Requires specialized indexing engines
Higher latency for initial indexing
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Use Vespa or Elasticsearch with native ColBERT support. 2) Use the PLAID engine for highly efficient late interaction inference. 3) Fine-tune the ColBERT model on your specific domain data using RAGatouille.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: While DeepSeek is a generation model, its strong embedding capabilities can be adapted or fine-tuned for late interaction setups in high-accuracy enterprise search.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen's dense embeddings can be used as the base for ColBERT-style late interaction, and Qwen2.5's strong generation ensures that the highly precise retrieved context is utilized perfectly.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's long context makes ColBERT less critical for single-doc search, but for massive corpus search, ColBERT's precision ensures the most relevant chunks are fed into Kimi's massive window.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM's embedding models can be integrated into Vespa for ColBERT setups, leveraging GLM-4's strong generation to synthesize the highly nuanced context retrieved by late interaction.

references: Khattab & Zaharia 2020 'ColBERT: Fast and Accurate Document Retrieval via PLaid Interaction'

eli5: It builds a map of connections like GraphRAG, but it's much faster and cheaper because it skips the heavy AI summarization and just uses smart shortcuts to find the answer.
purpose: Combine the relational reasoning of Graph RAG with the semantic flexibility of Vector RAG, but optimize for speed and cost by avoiding heavy LLM-based community detection.
input_dataset: Unstructured text requiring relational reasoning, but where the massive compute cost of Microsoft GraphRAG is prohibitive.
usecase_scenarios: Fast-paced enterprise search requiring relational context
Dynamic knowledge bases where the graph needs to be updated frequently
Applications needing GraphRAG capabilities but with strict latency and budget constraints
outcome: Fast, cost-effective retrieval that captures both specific entity details and broad relational themes.
benchmark_metrics: Indexing time and compute cost reduction

metadata.computational_complexity: O(N * L) for lightweight entity extraction, O(V + E) for dual-level traversal
pros: Drastically reduces indexing time and compute cost
Captures both micro and macro context
Highly scalable and easier to maintain
cons: Loses the deep 'community summaries' of traditional GraphRAG
Requires careful tuning of the dual-level retrieval weights
Still more complex to set up than pure Vector RAG
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Use the LightRAG library for out-of-the-box dual-level indexing. 2) Implement a routing mechanism: use low-level retrieval for specific entity queries, and high-level retrieval for thematic queries. 3) Use a fast, cheap LLM for the entity extraction phase.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-R1's reasoning can be used to intelligently route queries between the low-level (entity) and high-level (relational) retrieval paths, optimizing accuracy.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5-7B is the perfect model for LightRAG's entity extraction phase. It's fast, cheap, and accurate, keeping the indexing pipeline highly efficient.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's long context can easily absorb the combined outputs of both the low-level and high-level retrieval paths, ensuring no relational nuance is lost during generation.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's tool-use can dynamically decide whether a query requires low-level entity lookup or high-level relational traversal, acting as an intelligent router for LightRAG.

references: Han et al. 2024 'LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation'

eli5: Groups similar paragraphs together, summarizes them, and builds a tree of summaries from the bottom up, so the AI can search at the exact right level of detail.
purpose: Overcome the flat structure of standard vector stores by recursively clustering and summarizing text chunks into a tree, enabling both broad thematic retrieval and specific detail retrieval.
input_dataset: Large unstructured text corpora where documents contain multiple themes and sub-topics.
usecase_scenarios: Analyzing long-form journalism or books
Complex legal case files with multiple overlapping arguments
Scientific literature reviews covering multiple sub-fields
outcome: A hierarchical tree of text chunks and summaries, allowing the retriever to fetch high-level themes or low-level details depending on the query.
benchmark_metrics: Tree depth vs. retrieval latency trade-off

metadata.computational_complexity: O(N * L) for recursive summarization, O(log N) for tree traversal
pros: Natively handles documents with multiple distinct themes
Allows for both broad and highly specific retrieval
Reduces the 'lost in the middle' problem for long documents
cons: High compute cost for building the tree (requires many LLM summarization calls)
Clustering can sometimes group unrelated concepts if embeddings are poor
Complex to maintain and update incrementally
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Automate the tree-building process using LlamaIndex's RAPTOR module. 2) Use a fast, cheap model for the recursive summarization steps to keep costs down. 3) Implement a dual-retrieval strategy: search the leaf nodes for specific facts, and search the summary nodes for broad themes.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-V3's strong summarization ensures high-quality node summaries during the recursive clustering phase, preserving critical nuances.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5-7B is highly efficient for the repetitive clustering and summarization tasks required to build the RAPTOR tree, keeping costs low.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's massive context allows it to process larger clusters at once, reducing the depth of the tree and speeding up the indexing phase significantly.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's structured output ensures the clustering algorithms receive consistently formatted inputs during the tree-building phase, reducing parsing errors.

references: Sarthi et al. 2024 'RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval'

eli5: Instead of manually tweaking prompts and settings, you give an AI compiler your goals, and it automatically writes, tests, and optimizes the perfect RAG pipeline for you.
purpose: Automate the optimization of RAG pipelines (prompts, few-shot examples, retriever weights) using programmatic frameworks like DSPy, replacing manual prompt engineering with algorithmic optimization.
input_dataset: Unstructured text + a labeled validation set of queries and ideal answers.
usecase_scenarios: Enterprise RAG systems requiring continuous optimization as data changes
Teams lacking deep prompt engineering expertise
Complex pipelines with multiple LLM calls that are hard to tune manually
outcome: A mathematically optimized RAG pipeline with tuned prompts, few-shot examples, and routing logic, maximizing accuracy and minimizing token usage.
benchmark_metrics: Validation set accuracy (pre vs. post compilation)

metadata.computational_complexity: O(T * L) for compilation (where T is trials), O(1) for inference
pros: Drastically reduces manual prompt engineering time
Automatically finds optimal few-shot examples and instructions
Can jointly optimize retriever and generator components
cons: Requires a high-quality labeled validation set
Compilation can be computationally expensive and slow
Steep learning curve for the DSPy framework
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Define your RAG pipeline using DSPy Signatures and Modules. 2) Create a robust validation set with ground-truth answers. 3) Use DSPy's MIPRO or BootstrapFewShot optimizers to automatically compile the pipeline. 4) Deploy the compiled pipeline and set up automated re-compilation triggers when data drifts.

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-R1 can be used as the 'teacher' model in DSPy to generate high-quality bootstrap examples for optimizing the RAG pipeline.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5 is highly compatible with DSPy's optimizers, providing fast and accurate inference during the compilation and evaluation phases.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's long context is ideal for DSPy's evaluation steps, allowing it to process full retrieved contexts without truncation during optimization.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's strong instruction following makes it a reliable 'student' model that accurately learns and executes the optimized prompts generated by DSPy.

references: Khattab et al. 2023 'DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into State-of-the-Art Pipelines'

eli5: Instead of just searching text, it understands the actual code structure—functions, classes, and how they call each other—to find the exact code needed to fix a bug or add a feature.
purpose: Enhance retrieval for software repositories by combining text embeddings with Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) parsing, call graphs, and repository-level context.
input_dataset: Software codebases (GitHub repos, local directories) containing multiple languages and file types.
usecase_scenarios: AI-powered code editors and IDE plugins
Automated bug fixing and refactoring agents
Codebase Q&A for onboarding new developers
outcome: Highly precise code retrieval that understands dependencies, imports, and structural context, enabling accurate code generation and modification.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(N) for AST parsing and graph building, O(log N) for code search
pros: Understands code semantics, not just text similarity
Captures cross-file dependencies and imports
Drastically reduces hallucinated or syntactically invalid code
cons: Requires complex parsing infrastructure for multiple languages
High compute cost for building and maintaining the repo graph
AST structures can be massive, requiring aggressive pruning
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Use tree-sitter to parse code into ASTs for multiple languages. 2) Build a call graph and dependency map of the repository. 3) Generate a 'repo map' (a high-level summary of files and functions) to provide global context. 4) Retrieve specific code chunks based on the repo map and call graph relevance.
dependencies: Code Embedding Model (e.g., Voyage-Code, StarCoder Embed)
Graph Database or In-Memory Graph for Call Graphs

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-Coder-V2 is the undisputed leader here; its native understanding of code structure makes it perfect for generating and querying AST-based context.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5-Coder provides excellent code comprehension and can efficiently parse and embed code chunks for the vector index.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi's massive context allows it to ingest entire repository maps or large codebases directly, bypassing the need for complex chunking in smaller repos.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: CodeGeeX or GLM-4 can be used to generate the repository-level summaries and file-level context required for the indexing phase.

references: Yang et al. 2024 'SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering'

algorithm_name: Semantic Router RAG / Dynamic Pipeline Routing
eli5: A traffic cop for your AI. It looks at your question and instantly directs it to the best tool—whether that's a database search, a web search, or a document search.
purpose: Use a lightweight, ultra-fast classifier or embedding router to analyze incoming queries and dynamically route them to the most appropriate specialized RAG pipeline to optimize cost and accuracy.
input_dataset: Diverse query types targeting multiple specialized data sources (SQL DBs, Vector DBs, Graph DBs, Web APIs).
usecase_scenarios: Enterprise AI assistants that need to query both internal docs and live databases
Customer support bots handling both FAQ lookups and account-specific SQL queries
Complex research assistants combining web search and internal knowledge bases
outcome: Queries are automatically directed to the most efficient and accurate retrieval pipeline, reducing latency, token costs, and hallucination rates.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(1) for routing (using optimized ANN or simple dot product), O(Pipeline) for execution
pros: Drastically reduces costs by avoiding expensive LLM calls for simple queries
Improves accuracy by using specialized pipelines for specific query types
Highly scalable and modular architecture
cons: Requires maintaining multiple specialized pipelines
Routing errors can lead to completely wrong answers
Adds a small amount of latency to every request
metadata.implementation_guide: 1) Define your specialized RAG pipelines (e.g., SQL RAG, Vector RAG, Graph RAG). 2) Create a set of example utterances for each pipeline. 3) Use the Semantic Router library to embed these examples and create ultra-fast routing boundaries. 4) Implement a fallback mechanism for queries that don't match any route with high confidence.
dependencies: Semantic Router Library or Custom Classifier

model_specific_optimizations.deepseek: DeepSeek-V3's function calling can act as the semantic router, dynamically selecting the correct RAG sub-pipeline based on query intent with high accuracy.
model_specific_optimizations.qwen: Qwen2.5-7B can be fine-tuned as an ultra-fast, low-latency semantic router to classify queries before they hit the heavier RAG pipelines.
model_specific_optimizations.kimi: Kimi can act as the final synthesis engine, receiving the structured outputs from the various routed RAG pipelines and combining them seamlessly.
model_specific_optimizations.z_ai: GLM-4's fast inference makes it ideal for the routing layer, ensuring the query classification adds negligible latency to the overall pipeline.

references: Semantic Router Documentation
LangChain Documentation: Router Chains
metadata.code_snippet:
from semantic_router import Route, RouteLayer
from semantic_router.encoders import FastEmbedEncoder

# Define routes for different pipelines
sql_route = Route(name="sql_query", utterances=["What is the total revenue?", "Show me the top 5 users"])
vector_route = Route(name="doc_search", utterances=["What is the return policy?", "How does the algorithm work?"])

encoder = FastEmbedEncoder()
rl = RouteLayer(encoder=encoder, routes=[sql_route, vector_route])

# Route the query
query = "What is the total revenue for Q3?"
route_name = rl(query).name # Returns 'sql_query'
